summary.text: Annie Andrews is a pediatrician and the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate. She worked as a pediatric hospitalist at the Medical University of South Carolina and was the 2022 Democratic nominee in South Carolina's 1st Congressional District. She describes herself as a pediatrician and a mom, not a politician, and says she takes no corporate PAC money.

paragraphs.text: Born in 1981 in Paducah, Kentucky, and raised in Indianapolis, Indiana, according to Wikipedia.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Dayton, an M.D. from the University of Cincinnati and a master's degree in clinical research from the Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC).

Completed a pediatrics residency in Cincinnati, then moved to South Carolina's Lowcountry in 2009. She worked about 14 years at MUSC Children's Hospital in Charleston as a pediatric hospitalist and was a professor of pediatrics at MUSC.
According to her campaign website, she spent nearly two decades in children's hospitals before turning to advocacy and policy work on school safety, health-care access and abortion rights.
Became politically active after the 2018 Parkland shooting, joining Moms Demand Action and doing clinical research on firearm injury prevention in children.

Ran for Congress in South Carolina's 1st District in 2022, her first campaign; she was the Democratic nominee and lost to Rep. Nancy Mace, 56.5% to 42.5%. She resigned from MUSC in 2023 and started a PAC, Their Future. Our Vote.

Announced her U.S. Senate candidacy on May 29, 2025 and won the June 9, 2026 Democratic primary with 61.5% of the vote. She was running against Lindsey Graham until his death on July 11, 2026, and now faces Darline Graham.
Lives in Charleston with her three children, who attend public schools, according to her campaign website.
